brief: Nothing is alive in the air at night except the fireflies, and they never leave the lawn. Counted off the wide night frame (seed 42, t 432, hour 02.5): roughly forty lamps and lit windows across the picture — LANE_LAMPS, RIVER_LAMPS, the plaza and cross-street lamps, BARGE_LAMP, the rose window — and not one of them has anything at it. Give the town a nocturnal species with its OWN source and its own cap, gathered AT the light rather than scattered over the frame, so that the night reads as inhabited from the wide shot and not merely lit. It must answer the pointer the way every bird already does. Why now: People & animals is 14 iterations back, the longest neglect in the run, and its last entry (#161) was a rejected brief; the night is simultaneously the town's best-looking state and its emptiest.
successLooksLike: On a night frame at 1600x950 the lamps have life at them and it is legible without zooming; the pointer names it; the population is zero in full daylight and non-zero on every night sampled across a seeded year; `speciesKinds` moves in the census and the baseline is re-pinned.
avoid: Do not spend the vector on a second firefly — a scatter over an area is what already exists. This one is bound to the LIGHTS. Do not take the spawn out of an existing budget: LAWS says a spawn band is a share of a budget, not a rate, so a rare thing needs its OWN source. Bound the population at BOTH ends (a window with only a landing bound is a marathon-walker factory), and key it on `sunUp`/`nightF` correctly — `!daylight` is dawn as well as dusk, and `day` rolls at hour 6 so it holds two dawns.
